'''''Iresine diffusa''''', or '''Juba's bush''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=IRDI|taxon=Iresine diffusa|accessdate=25 May 2015}}</ref> is a species of plant in the family [[Amaranthaceae]]. Its form ''Iresine diffusa'' f. ''lindenii'', formerly ''Iresine lindenii'', is commercially available as an ornamental.<ref name="POWO_129901-2" >{{cite POWO |id=129901-2 |title=''Iresine diffusa'' f. ''lindenii'' (Van Houtte) L.B.Sm. & Downs |access-date=10 May 2023 }}</ref><ref name="RHS_41191" >{{cite web |title=''Iresine lindenii'' blood leaf |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/41191/iresine-lindenii/details |date=2023 |publisher=The Royal Horticultural Society |access-date=10 May 2023 }}</ref>
[[File:Iresine lindenii kz1.jpg|thumb|left|Planting of ''Iresine diffusa'' f. ''lindenii'']]

==Appearance== 
Herb 1–2 m, stem a little grooved, nodes jointed.  Leaves opp, 14 x 7 cm, edge smooth.  Flowers minute, greenish-white, panicle 40 cm long, male more open, female compact, 1 mm.  Seed 0.5 mm.<ref>[http://www.conabio.gob.mx/malezasdemexico/amaranthaceae/iresine-diffusa/fichas/pagina1.htm conabio]</ref>

==Folk use==
It is used to treat ovary inflammation in Peru.<ref>{{cite journal | pmid = 21040536 | doi=10.1186/1746-4269-6-30 | volume=6 | title=Medicinal plants used in Northern Peru for reproductive problems and female health | pmc=2984435 | year=2010 | journal=J Ethnobiol Ethnomed | article-number=30  | last1 = Bussmann | first1 = RW | last2 = Glenn | first2 = A | doi-access = free }}</ref>

==Chemistry==
Drimenes in aerial parts.<ref>{{cite journal | pmid = 15674810 | doi=10.1002/mrc.1550 | volume=43 | title=1H and 13C assignments of three new drimenes from Iresine diffusa Humb. & Bonpl. ex Willd | year=2005 | journal=Magn Reson Chem | pages=339–42  | last1 = Rios | first1 = MY | last2 = Berber | first2 = LA | issue=4 }}</ref>
